$comment: Accepted-problem baseline for scripts/check-railway-deploy-drift.mjs.
The drift check fails on any service that is not running everything that can
reach it and is NOT listed here. An entry means: this service is knowingly
behind, it has an owner issue, and it must not page again until that issue moves.
Entries are matched on service:verdict exactly, and the split is the same one
scripts/check-seed-freshness.mjs applies to compact health -- same function, so
expiry and prune-on-recovery cannot drift into two different meanings.
A service that recovers is reported as 'recovered' on the next run (prune it).
A service that fails with a DIFFERENT verdict than the one baselined blocks,
which is the point: BEHIND on a service baselined for REJECTED_PUSH is a new
failure wearing an old name.
This file held 62 REJECTED_PUSH entries -- every service carrying a Railway
watch-path filter -- until #6142. They were not degradations: the check demanded
that a FILTERED service run HEAD, which under a watch-path filter is not the
healthy state. Re-measured across the fleet, 7,331 of 7,391 path-reason skips
were plainly correct and the other 60 are explained (build context, and a
registry closure not yet applied to Railway). The check is now closure-aware and
reports CURRENT_FOR_CLOSURE for those services instead, so the entries are gone
rather than suppressed. Do not re-add them: a REJECTED_PUSH today means Railway
refused a push that DID reach the service, which is a real failure.
expiresAt forces a re-review of the whole file. A stale-deploy suppression that
outlives its cause is how a fleet ends up silently a week behind.

acknowledged.name: umami
acknowledged.reason: The analytics collector stopped receiving deployments from the GitHub integration on 2026-08-03. Its watch paths are already empty, so this is the webhook-side sibling of #6141 rather than a filter rejection -- and the failure that proves this check must not key on the filter: no SKIPPED record exists, and the service is a day behind head.
